title: Refuse a multi-line paste into the secret prompt: drain and flush, and point docs at the file or stdin route (DEC-255 (a2)(3))

acceptanceCriteria.text: When input is still queued after the terminator, the prompt refuses with a plain error, then drains and flushes the queued input, and no queued byte reaches a later prompt or the shell
The refusal is consistent with the bound refusal in secret-value.ts
The docs point multi-line secrets to the file or stdin route

implementationNotes: Built to DEC-255 (a2)(3). src/adapters/secret-value.ts: after a hidden read returns a non-empty value, a new inputPending part (default inputQueued(0) in terminal-input.ts: isatty, then poll for one quiet interval, POLLIN with no ERR/HUP/NVAL) decides; queued input throws WardError secret_value_multiline (new catalog entry, validation, hint points at --stdin), and the existing finally drains and flushes before echo returns. An empty or Ctrl-C read is not judged as a paste. AC3 wording: no docs page for secret set exists in this checkout (docs/ holds ADRs, runbooks and security-tests only), so the pointer is in the manifest's secret summary (what ward help secret prints) and the error hint; the plugin skill was not touched. Evidence: bun run check green (1162 pass); real-pty scenarios in test/pty-residue.test.ts now expect REFUSED:secret_value_multiline for both the short and the past-the-queue paste with nothing reaching the shell, and a new one-line scenario still reads LEN:6.

Opus review of opum-ai/ward-cli#253 recorded as written. Unit: ward-cli-review-253 (transcript model claude-opus-5-5 on all 32 turns, per the leader). Head: 75aa331. Worktree: review-253-75aa331.

VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES
HEAD: 75aa331

Review of opum-ai/ward-cli#253 (WCLI-134, DEC-255 (a2)(3)). I read every file in the diff plus the code around it. I could not run anything.

FINDINGS:

1. MEDIUM, src/adapters/terminal-input.ts:144-150 and src/adapters/secret-value.ts:180. Ward can store the first line of a multi-line paste even after its own drain has seen the rest of that paste.
   - `inputQueued` decides from a single 30 ms poll (QUIET_MS). The `finally` then calls `flushPendingInput` (:187-205), which runs tcflush, then `drainPending`. The drain opens a fresh 30 ms poll window after the probe's and keeps flushing for up to 1.5 s (DRAIN_BUDGET_MS).
   - So when the rest of a paste arrives between about 30 ms and 1.5 s after the terminator (iTerm2 Paste Slowly, ssh or mosh over a slow link, a flow-controlled writer), Ward flushes those bytes itself. Meanwhile `readHidden` has already returned the first line, and `setSecret` stores it.
   - Ward is holding direct evidence of a multi-line paste and still stores a prefix. The bound refusal exists to prevent exactly that: "a stored prefix of a larger value would be a silently wrong secret" (secret-value.ts:88-92). That makes this an AC1 gap ("when input is still queued after the terminator… refuses").
   - `flushPendingInput` returns void, so the drain cannot report what it saw.
   - Cheap fix: have the drain return whether it flushed anything (count only flushes after a POLLIN, not the unconditional first tcflush). Refuse on true, while still inside the finally before `setRaw(false)`, or restructure so the drain runs before the return. The refusal window then equals the discard window.
   - No test covers this. The pty harness sends each paste in one `stdin.write`, so nothing ever stalls past 30 ms.

2. LOW, terminal-input.ts:147. A failed poll counts as "nothing queued".
   - `polled.result <= 0` treats a negative result (EINTR, for example from a SIGWINCH during a window resize) as no queued input, so the probe fails open on one attempt.
   - `drainPending` in the same file retries `result < 0` within its deadline (:171).
   - It is rare, but these sibling functions are inconsistent: the drain retries and the refusal gives up. Retry within a short deadline, the way the drain does.

3. LOW, secret-value.ts:180-181. The refused value is never zeroed.
   - The throw drops `value`, the first line of the paste. That line is plausibly real secret material, for example a token followed by a stray line.
   - `setSecret`'s `finally { value?.fill(0) }` (src/application/secrets.ts:431) never sees it, because `readHidden` threw before the assignment.
   - Add `value.fill(0)` before the throw.
   - The unzeroed `number[]` inside `readHiddenValueBytes` on the too_large path predates this PR and is not charged to it.

4. LOW, secret-value.ts:100 combined with :180. A one-line value can be refused as a multi-line paste.
   - `readHiddenValueBytes` stops on `\r` and leaves anything after it queued.
   - If the clipboard holds a value copied from a CRLF file (`token\r\n`), or the terminal sends CRLF on Enter (an LNM, telnet or serial-style client), the lone `\n` stays queued. The value is then refused as `secret_value_multiline`.
   - The hint then tells the user to "Enter a one-line value", which they already did. Before this PR, that `\n` was silently flushed.
   - This fails closed, so it is not a leak, but it is a confusing false refusal. Fix: consume a single `\n` directly after a `\r` terminator before probing.

5. LOW (coverage), test/pty-residue.test.ts:28-43 and test/secret.test.ts:977-1004. CI never exercises the real probe's "queued" result.
   - `scenario()` skips every pty case off darwin, and CI runs on `[self-hosted, Linux, ARM64]`.
   - In CI, the unit test stubs `inputPending`, and the only real-probe test ("not a terminal") returns at `isatty` before the poll.
   - So if `inputQueued`'s post-isatty logic were mutated to always return false (or always true), every CI check would still pass. AC1's real-tty proof, including the LEN:6 accepting control, rests entirely on a local darwin run.
   - Not a blocker under the existing harness rule, but it should be stated in the AC1 evidence rather than implied by "bun run check green".

6. NIT, src/contract/manifest.ts:373 and src/contract/errors.ts:296. Both texts claim more than the code guarantees.
   - The manifest says a multi-line paste "is refused". The error message says Ward "discarded what was queued".
   - Both are best-effort: the refusal never fires where poll is unresolved, and per #1 it covers only a 30 ms window. The drain is capped at 1.5 s.
   - The comment at terminal-input.ts:142-143 says "best-effort narrowing". A small qualifier in the user-facing text ("is refused when it is detected", "discarded what was queued at the time") would keep the two honest.

7. NIT, .quest/tasks/WCLI-134.json. The record is still `"status":"To Do"` at the head commit, although it already carries implementation notes.

Brief items checked and found sound (not findings):
- Item 1, fail-open:
  - The non-tty branch cannot be reached from `readHidden`, because the `isInteractive` gate (`process.stdin.isTTY`) implies `isatty(0)`.
  - If poll is unresolved, the refusal never fires and `flushPendingInput` warns once (:196). That is acceptable best effort under the ruling's wording.
  - Bytes sitting in Bun's own stdin buffer are not a shell-leak path. `readHiddenValueBytes` uses `readSync` with a 1-byte buffer, so there is no userspace read-ahead, and any such buffer dies with the process.
  - The ERR/HUP/NVAL handling is correct: a hung-up or invalid descriptor is not a paste.
- Item 2, the value on refusal:
  - The value never reaches the error. The catalog takes no message argument (errors.ts:3-5), and the code is thrown with no details.
  - The refusal follows the same rethrow path as `secret_value_too_large` (catch at :188), so the flush runs before `setRaw(false)` in the existing finally. The unit test asserts ["raw:on","flush","raw:off"] on the refusal.
  - "Stored nothing" is accurate. On the replace path, `confirmReplace` runs before the read (secrets.ts:371) and the vault mutate comes after it.
- Item 3, empty and Ctrl-C reads:
  - The `value.length > 0` guard is correct. An empty read, an abandoned read, or a leading-newline paste falls through to `secret_value_rejected` with the flush still run.
  - The probe-before-flush order is the only order that works. There is no ordering hazard.
  - Covered by the unit test's abandoned case and the pty Ctrl-C LEN:0 case.
- Items 4 and 1 (AC2 consistency and the AC3 wording):
  - AC2: the error has the same type (validation, so the same exit class), the same throw-inside-the-try path and the same flush as the bound refusal.
  - AC3: "pipe a multi-line secret in with --stdin, for example from a file" is accurate. --stdin reads exact bytes through EOF and refuses a tty, and there is no separate file route. One minor point the docs leave out: a file's trailing newline is stored as part of the value, since nothing is stripped.
- Item 5, the tests: the real-pty refusal cases do prove nothing reaches the shell. The shell's next read is RESULT:AFTER, no LEAK marker appears anywhere, and the long-tail case shows the drain held. The one-line LEN:6 scenario is a real accepting control on darwin.

UNVERIFIED:
- Whether "bun run check green (1162 pass)" and the darwin pty scenarios actually ran and passed at 75aa331. I have no shell, and CI skips the pty cases.
- That the drain in #1 would actually see bytes arriving 30 ms to 1.5 s late on a real pty. That follows from reading the code; I did not measure it.
- The real-world frequency of CRLF on Enter (#4), and Bun's process.stdin behaviour (no read-ahead before readSync), beyond what the passing pty scenarios imply.

Fixes for the REQUEST CHANGES at 75aa331, as new commits on #253. (1) The drain now reports whether it flushed input after a POLLIN (drainPending and flushPendingInput return a boolean; the unconditional first tcflush is not counted); readHidden refuses on that result as well as on the probe, after the flush and after setRaw(false) has run, so the refusal window equals the discard window. (2) The queue probe (queuedInput) retries a failed poll within a 150 ms deadline instead of reading it as nothing queued. (3) The refused first line is zeroed before the throw. (4) A line feed directly behind a carriage-return terminator is consumed; any other byte behind a return is refused as a paste. (5) Evidence limit, stated plainly: CI runs on Linux and the pty scenarios in test/pty-residue.test.ts are darwin-only, so the real-tty proof (the refusal cases, the stalled-tail case and the LEN:6 one-line accepting control) comes from a local darwin run, not from CI; CI covers the stubbed unit cases and the poll-binding cases only, and does not exercise inputQueued's real queued result. (6) The user-facing text now claims what the code does: the manifest says a multi-line paste is refused when it is detected, and the error says what was queued at the time was discarded. (7) Status set to In Progress. Optional item taken: the manifest text now says a file's trailing newline is stored as part of the value with --stdin.
Evidence at the fix head: bun run check green; unit cases for the drain's report, the probe's retry and deadline, the late-tail refusal (flush returns true, probe false: refused, order raw:on, flush, raw:off, first line zeroed), a flush that reports nothing leaving a one-line value accepted, and CRLF; a new pty scenario sends the first line then the tail 45 ms later and expects REFUSED:secret_value_multiline with nothing reaching the shell (run 5 times locally on darwin, 5 passes). Mutation controls, each run and restored: refusal ignoring the late drain turns the unit and pty stalled-tail cases red; a drain that never reports turns the pty case and the drain unit case red; a probe that does not retry turns its unit case red; not consuming the CRLF line feed turns the CRLF case red; not zeroing turns the two zeroing cases red.
